title: Platform teams and golden paths: the standard that gets adopted because it is easier

videos.script: Most companies get a platform team the same way. Somebody notices that seven teams have built seven deploy pipelines, and decides there should be one. {{seven}} The usual next step is a rule. A standard is written, and every team is told to use it. A year later, some of those teams have quietly found a way around it, and nobody hears why. {{rule}} This lesson takes the other route. A platform team treats the other engineers as its customers. It builds the supported way of doing a common task, and it makes that way the easiest one. Spotify calls it a golden path. {{path}} At Coreto, Rafaela Nunes leads the Platform team. Her service template was never compulsory. In its first year, eighteen of the twenty-six new services started from it anyway. {{template}} By the end of the lesson you can say what a platform team is for and what belongs on a golden path. You can also tell a standard that teams adopted from one they only obey. {{adoption}}
